questions.question: Explain how food preparation is treated as a manufacturing process, identify the inputs, resources and output for the pilchard relish, and list its steps as instructions.
questions.expected_answer: A kitchen is a small factory: raw materials come in, processes such as washing, opening, chopping, heating, stirring and seasoning act on them, and plates of food go out, so the preparation is planned as a sequence of manufacture with steps in order, each with a time, tools and a person, and the order matters even more than for the crane because food spoils, burns and poisons. For the relish for ten the inputs are two tins of pilchards in tomato sauce, a tin of tomatoes, two onions, a tablespoon of oil, salt and curry powder; the resources are a pot, burner, knife, board, tin opener, wooden spoon, ladle and bowls; the output is ten portions of 150 grams, steaming hot, with soft onion and a sauce that coats the spoon. Steps: wash hands with soap; wipe the surface; collect ingredients and equipment; peel and chop the onions; heat the oil on medium; fry the onions until soft, about five minutes; open and add the tomato tin; open the pilchard tins and add gently with their sauce; add salt and curry powder; simmer stirring for ten minutes; taste and adjust; check it is steaming hot; serve with pap; wash up.

questions.question: Describe how the steps are ordered, and state the hygiene steps and the safety rules for knives, tins and heat that must appear as steps on the chart.
questions.expected_answer: Steps are ordered by dependency and time: hands washed before anything is touched and again after raw food and before serving; surface wiped before food is placed; onions chopped before the oil is hot; tins opened just before they are added so open food does not stand in the warm; water for pap set to boil first because it takes longest, with pap and relish in parallel columns meeting at serving. Hygiene steps: wash hands with soap and clean water for twenty seconds before cooking, after the toilet, after raw food and before serving; use clean water for cooking and washing vegetables; keep raw and ready food on separate boards and in separate bowls; cover waiting food; serve hot food steaming, above 60 degrees, within two hours of cooking; wash pots and spoons in hot soapy water. Safety: cut on a board with the blade away from the body and fingers curled under, put the knife down flat and never leave it in washing water; open tins fully and lift the lid by its edge without running a finger round the rim; turn pot handles away from the walkway, lift with a dry cloth, raise lids away from the face, fill pots no more than two thirds, and keep children and crowding away from the burner, with a named person responsible for each hot or sharp step.

questions.question: Describe how the flow chart for the food item is drawn, timed against the period and rehearsed with roles, and name the readiness tests it must contain.
questions.expected_answer: It is drawn with an oval for start, rectangles for every step carrying a verb, a time and the responsible person's initials, diamonds for the readiness tests with no arrows looping back, onions soft to fry longer, tastes seasoned to add salt or spice, steaming hot and simmered ten minutes to continue simmering, and an oval for end at serving; two items cooked together are two columns, pap on the left starting with boiling water, relish on the right, joined by arrows into one serve box, drawn with a ruler and square corners. Times are added up each column, relish about thirty minutes and pap about forty, so pap starts ten minutes earlier, and if the total exceeds the period the plan is shortened by chopping while water boils, using the tin's own sauce or serving as soon as hot, with washing up as a final shared box. Four roles are assigned, pap, relish, hygiene and serving, safety and washing up, and the team walks through the chart with each person pointing at their boxes, checking that no two people need the knife or burner at once, moving any clashing box and adding any missing tool. The chart goes into the folder and comes to the kitchen as the recipe card.
